rv.q: Blaney and Harrison are pungently entertaining, even if both lean a little towards caricature. Blaney, in his moth-eaten jumper, tweedy coat and muffler, has a tic of preciously touching his throat, as if fretting about protecting the invaluable instrument that is his voice.
Superb acting, design and direction, plus really fine writing make for a drama that is much more than the sum of its parts.
Though it could go further in places, it's still an absorbing watch.

cn.t: David Ireland's punchy debut play impresses with its sharp humor and provocative themes, though some find its brief structure messy and rushed. Critics praise its perceptive take on human nature despite uneven execution.
